package_info.package_manager: CDN (not a package manager, but a third-party JavaScript CDN service)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served after February 2024 (post-acquisition by Funnull)
package_info.why_malicious: The CDN service began serving malicious, obfuscated JavaScript payloads that dynamically inject code into websites, enabling user redirection, evasion of detection, and potentially broader attacks such as formjacking and data exfiltration. The service is no longer trustworthy and is actively used as a supply chain attack vector.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website loading polyfill.io script)
execution_context.file_location: Served dynamically from cdn.polyfill.io (injected into the HTML <script> tag)
required_permissions: potentially access to user input fields

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for admin users and analytics scripts, then after a delay, injects a script tag loading a fake Google Analytics script from a typo-squatted domain, resulting in user redirection to malicious sites.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code dynamically injects a script from a domain that closely mimics a legitimate analytics provider but is misspelled, a classic phishing and redirection tactic. The use of obfuscation, conditional execution, and delayed payload delivery are all hallmarks of evasive malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill service is expected to serve static, open-source, standards-compliant JavaScript for browser compatibility—not to inject third-party scripts, perform user targeting, or redirect users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or A/B testing scripts may dynamically inject scripts, but always from trusted, well-known domains and with transparent user consent.
key_indicators: Dynamic script injection from typo-squatted domains
Conditional execution based on user/device/analytics presence
Redirection to unrelated, potentially harmful sites

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website loading polyfill.io script)
execution_context.file_location: Served dynamically from cdn.polyfill.io (injected into the HTML <script> tag)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code inspects HTTP headers and user environment to selectively activate malicious payloads, targeting mobile devices and avoiding admin or analytics environments, enabling targeted redirection or future data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Selective activation based on device type and environment is a common evasion technique, allowing the malware to avoid detection by security researchers and automated scanners.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Polyfill scripts should not perform environment reconnaissance or selectively execute based on user/device context.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Feature detection for browser compatibility is legitimate, but not for evasion or targeting.

attack_chain.action: Website includes <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/...">, loading the malicious JavaScript from the CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript inspects the environment (user agent, HTTP headers, presence of analytics/admin).
attack_chain.leads_to: Conditional activation of the malicious payload.

attack_chain.action: If conditions are met (e.g., mobile device, not admin, no analytics), the code delays execution and injects a script tag pointing to a fake analytics domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to malicious sites or further payloads are loaded.

attack_chain.action: User is redirected to sports betting, pornographic, or other malicious sites, or potentially exposed to further attacks (formjacking, data theft, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: user compromise, data theft, or monetization via redirects.

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic script injection from domains similar to legitimate analytics providers (e.g., googie-anaiytics.com)
Obfuscated JavaScript served from a previously trusted CDN
Conditional execution based on user agent, admin status, or analytics presence
file_indicators: Injected <script> tags with src pointing to typo-squatted analytics domains
network_indicators: Redirects to sports betting, pornographic, or other suspicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan website source code and network traffic for references to cdn.polyfill.io and typo-squatted analytics domains. Monitor for unexpected script injections and outbound requests to suspicious domains. Use browser instrumentation or web application firewalls to detect delayed script execution and conditional payload delivery. Flag obfuscated JavaScript served from third-party CDNs, especially if it performs environment checks or dynamic script injection.
